previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, alcohol abuse, dementia, recurrent aspiration, and atrial fibrillation was admitted for shortness of breath, fever, and hypotension. He was found to have septic shock due to aspiration pneumonia, requiring ICU admission, vasopressor support, and broad-spectrum antibiotics. He improved rapidly, was weaned off oxygen, and transitioned to oral amoxicillin-clavulanate. His hyponatremia resolved with fluid therapy, and he was restarted on home medications. A Foley catheter was managed with daily voiding trials, and he was discharged to extended care with plans for outpatient speech and swallow therapy, urology follow-up, and repeat endoscopy for a known esophageal ulcer.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with history of alcohol abuse, multiple recent 
hospitalizations who was admitted with hypoxia and hypotension 
attributed to aspiration pneumonia. He was initially in the ICU 
and required pressors and anemia requiring PRBCs. He was started 
on Vancomycin/Zosyn with improvement in his symptoms and called 
out to the medical floor. He was also found to have significant 
aspiration and on discussion accepts risk of aspiration.

# Shortness of Breath ___ Aspiration PNA vs. Acute Pulmonary 
Edema vs. COPD exacerbation: The patient presented with hypoxia 
and was in the ICU with hypotension which briefly required 
pressors. He was initially on Vancomycin/Zosyn, narrowed to 
Ceftriaxone on ___. However, broadened back to Vanc/Zosyn ___ 
after WBC was noted to be rising. Through course of admission, 
he had recurrent episodes of shortness of breath which were felt 
most likely related to recurrent aspirations. In addition, there 
was felt to be a possible component of COPD exacerbation with 
wheezing on exam as well as mild pulmonary edema with rales on 
exam and elevated BNP. He will continue vanc/zosyn for a total 8 
day course for HCAP (last day = ___. Of note, vanc dose was 
decreased to 750 q 12 (from 1000 q 12) on ___ for vanc 
trough of 21. Vanc trough should be rechecked on ___ with 
dose adjusted accordingly. He was also treated for possible COPD 
component with 7 day steroid burst (last day ___. He was 
treated for volume overload with IV Lasix boluses. Volume status 
was somewhat difficult to monitor given urinary incontinence 
after Foley removal. Weights should be trended at rehab and IV 
Lasix PRN (40 mg) given for volume overload. Respiratory status 
improved and had been stable (satt'ing well on 2L) for several 
days at the time of discharge. Of note, CXR did raise concern 
for underlying ILD (see report above). Would refer for 
outpatient pulmonary evaluation.

# Dysphagia/Aspiration
# Goals of care
Discussed with the patient and his brother/HCP on multiple 
occasions. They both clearly state that the patient does NOT 
want a feeding tube. They understand the risks of aspiration. We 
also discussed code status and the patient's brother/HCP 
confirms he is DNR/DNI. A MOLST form was filled out. While 
patient is DNR/DNI and accepts risks of recurrent aspiration, he 
does wish for rehospitalization in the event of another PNA. 
Palliative care was involved in goals of care discussions.

# Leukocytosis: WBC had improved, but then uptrended again on 
the day of discharge. Afebrile. No new concerns on exam. Likely 
represents known ongoing aspirations; however, there could also 
be a component of hemoconcentration, as all cell lines were up. 
CXR was checked and showed no new process. 

# Paroxysmal Atrial fibrillation
Patient had an episode of atiral fibrillation with rapid rate 
prior to transfer to the ICU. His metoprolol was initially held 
in the setting of hypotension and was resumed ultimately. Pt did 
have intermittent episodes of afib throughout admission. He was 
in SR on the day of discharge. 

# Hyponatremia
Initially, attributed to SIADH with some component of 
hypovolemia. However, later in admission, it was felt that 
hyponatremia was likely related to SIADH (urine lytes consistent 
with this) with a component of volume overload. Sodium had 
improved with diuresis and free water restriction; however, 
trended down slightly again on the day of discharge. Sodium 
should be rechecked on ___ to ensure stability. Pt remains 
on 1200 cc free water restriction. Sodium was 128 on the day of 
discharge.

# Urinary retention
Seen in ___ clinic ___ after failed voiding trial on 
previous admission. At that time seems foley had been removed. 
___ was initially placed this admission but was successfully 
removed.

# Alcohol abuse
No longer drinking as he has been in rehab. Continued MVI, 
thiamine, folate.

# Anemia
Had H/H drop but responded to PRBCs and now stable. No signs of 
active bleeding. H/H remained stable thereafter.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with shortness of breath. This was felt to 
likely be related to pneumonia from your aspiration. There may 
have also been an underlying COPD component as well as fluid in 
your lungs. You were treated for all of these things.

of aspiration (which can lead to pneumonia, respiratory failure,
